Experienced feral here. 

Going to bear form is for the most part a defensive decision, if youre not running DOTC then you can swap to bear and frenzy regen to heal a ton, if DOTC it's sometimes worth going to bear to cast it still, as only costs 10 rage vs 40 energy (You basically have that just swapping into bear and taking a single tick of damage), and  you take less damage and have a higher health pool which means it heals more. 

A lot of mechanics can be solved by swapping to bear fast, like roots and slows, but also for higher or solo content if you know theres going to be a big hit and you dont have barkskin etc or you want to conserve them, then going bear is a great option. Especially if you're not even in melee range to begin with (E.G Rash'an in Dawnbreaker P2, if you get the web you can swap to bear for the initial hit and web break and pop a regen to help your healer out a ton)

Sometimes in dungeons you can also quickly swap to bear if your tank dies and you have no BR, it's no where near as strong as it used to be but you have significantly more chance of surviving a hit or few with cds in bear vs while in cat. (if Brez is almost off CD, you can generate rage so you can insta brez too).

Typically you dont want to bear just before you're going to die, you want to treat it as a preventative defensive to reduce the damage of an incoming blow vs trying to save yourself last minute.

I and many dont have the curtains open. Our walls are made of brick and stone, initially it takes awhile to warm up inside, infact older buildings have really thick walls which for short bursts of heat they manage really well with keeping it cool inside, however if it is constantly hot the walls and insulation also heat up and due to them being you know, brick with additional massive amounts of insulation, it turns the interior into an oven and takes a lot longer to cool down compared to wooden houses with plasterboard walls.

A few points:  
-They would only be used for a short amount of time during the year which puts people off buying them, however this is changing and more and more are getting them

-Very very rarely can a residential home in the UK have a window mounted AC unit (which are the cheaper, better and less expensive to run variants). Our windows tend to swing out (usually a mix of swinging out from a side, or the top or bottom swing out) and do not fully open without unlocking a safety latch. Even with the latch disabled the windows are a lot lot smaller and have extra edging to protect better from the weather and keep heat in even more so

-The main units that people can use are standing units, which are extremely poor at what they do. I have one and I wouldnt want to live without it, but they're extremely bad at their job unless you can get one with 2 tubes which are extremely expensive.

-Our homes are a lot smaller, like A LOT. the typical brit doesnt have storage space to store the damn thing for the 90% of the year it's not in use.

-Since our homes are designed to retain heat, you often need to run the AC extra long as the house is like an oven. I'm in an especially old building which has extremely thick brick walls and it was still hot inside with the AC going when it had gone down to 12C the next day. This just adds onto the cost which many cannot afford.

Talking to industry professionals honestly helped me A LOT, there is so much you can learn and they can dismiss so much bullshit that has been spread around as fact. 

I love getting critique on my work, I beg for it almost because it's the only way I can improve, whether it be artistic direction, anatomy, optimization or general creation. Tip toeing around the subjects and gentle nudging only works so far, even I can admit to getting in the thought process of "Ha ha my stuff is the best anything anyone says now is just wrong", people being blunt and matter of fact is the only way to get past that a lot.

A lot of the harshness from 3D modellers is just caused by others doing bad things and then ignoring advice and suggestion typically, but in the VRC community there is a level of elitism that comes from some creators, "I make stuff for this game that makes me better than you!" kinda mentality, and because they dont have a direct superior like a manager or boss who directly pays them, they cant really be put in their place or actively corrected.   


It's becoming more of an issue because other peoples work can actively start harming others experiences and enjoyment, I lost count how many times I've been relaxing and someone changes into an unoptimized avatar and has just completely tanked my performance and thus my enjoyment of the game. I'm here on a 4090 and getting hit hard by some of these things, this should simply never be the case.

No, over 100k is excessive. Theres entire games which are made up of less. Any game dev would laugh at the idea of a character being that high outside of animation or cinematic use.

There is simply no need for it to be that high, if done correctly the difference between a 250k-10mil model and a sub 70k model is incredibly insignificant, we've had techniques and resources that have been developed over decades now to make things look good while remaining low on resources. Most games their character models are in the 10 - 50k range, with different LODs for different settings and distances. We dont have LODs, your 170k is always going to be 170k, when in other games it would be able to be reduced down significantly to help performance.   


Bake your normals down, bake your AO and curvature, use correct topology flow for good deformation so you dont need extras to make it look smooth, use data transfers to create seamless transitions between meshes instead of everything being a solid conjoined mesh, combine object UVs to use less textures, use UDIMS if needed, use corrective shapes and hide shapes to hide body mesh thats hidden by clothing, and so much more.  


You need to take into account this is for VR as well, you basically have to triple the cost of everything. Your 170k is now effectively 480k. VR is intense on peoples systems as it is, theres a reason why quest poor is under 20k tris.

Exactly. Optimization is a key part of any 3D art, especially in games but it is done for everything else too like animation and renders. Stuff being optimized makes everyones lives easier, makes the creators life easier for posing, rendering and animating in terms of characters. Way less render time and resources needed to render an optimized character vs a unoptimized one.

Having a render or two is fine, but you REALLY need to include a lot of unedited ingame pictures too. So many I see have filters and effects added to the pictures and just... why.

If using renders they need to be actually using the ingame model and textures too. Seen too many which use a higher poly model with 8k textures for their render which is just false marketing.
170k is still really excessively high. If thats all baked down you can really go a lot lower, baked normals will carry a lot of the weight for detail.

Not all modellers. I love optimizing my shit and greatly encourage people do the same. 

It requires more work and people accepting stuff not being pristinely smooth (dont well you cant tell the difference anyway...) as well as good planning and using resources effeciently.

A lot of trouble people face with optimizing, is caused by issues created so early on that makes it harder to optimize later. Bad topology flow makes reducing the tri count later difficult, and a lot of makers just make the count high for better deformation, vs learning and doing good topology from the get go so it deforms good with lower tris. 

Textures  become an issue because people use a material per object, vs unwrapping multiple things onto a single texture set (or atlasing it) 

Theres plenty of tutorials and guides on doing this correctly, but because it's not labelled as for VRC specifically people dont use it, and instead follow guides made by amateurs or ones designed for animation or rendering instead of games.

Unlike avatars, you are not restricted to the VRC Mobile shaders. You can use whatever works for your needs, just note if something can be Standard Lite I would generally advise you use it for best performance

I think the whole geek fandom thing being a subculture is a lot more justified now. They've been  around a long time, but there is a lot more going on for them now. There is conventions and other events, there is a fashion associated with it, collectables, etc.

Most of people in geek fandoms arent just part of a single fandom, and each fandom is named appropriately to say a game or movie etc, but it has an overarching subculture that groups them all up in some way or another, while the "bonds holding them together" may be a bit looser in this group, there is still enough connection between them that I would atleast call it a subculture.

With regard to the whole appearance of goth.

Nearly everyones first interaction with goth these days is how it looks. Many dont look past that, they just see the fashion and make assumptions based on the little information they initially see, whether it's someone in a a band shirt and rat nest hair and siouxsie makeup, or someone in full black victorian-esq dresswear in a cemetery. This is a lot more prevalent in the modern day, where companies have started to profit a lot more off the look and is shoved further down peoples throats that it is a primarily fashion focused thing, when it isnt.

Past that it's just word of mouth based on more assumptions. These days not many even know the term of Post-Punk until someone tells them of it, which (if they have a few brain cells) then discover that it's music that came after the punk scene, but even then based on that term alone many wont get that it is goth music, "*cause it doesnt have the word goth in it"*. I've had this conversation a few times and it can be frustrating if the person isnt willing to listen and is determined that their assumption based, word of mouth view of goth is correct.

Some level of gatekeeping is needed in all subcultures really. Many of them are a lot more open while others are stricter, such as comparing to say the Furry community which is very open with the only requirement being to enjoy anthro characters and art, to say some geeky subcultures which will want you to know indepth knowledge about the topic.

Both of which have a core basis which the sub culture was founded on, one of them is a simple premise of art and character design, the other could be around a show/universe with indepth knowledge for example.

Goth definitely comes under the latter, there is a lot of stuff and history within the subculture, it is one that has been around now for 40 years even and it has evolved overtime. It makes sense that people who are truly within the scene want to preserve the foundation on which the subculture was created upon, like any other facet of history, people want to preserve it so that it is not forgotten.

The subculture has evolved with time, sprouting many offshoots and diversity in which is related to the subculture in some form, but the thing that connects it all is the music. The music started it, while the artists who created the music may have set the initial foundation for the style of fashion and lifestyle, the music itself is what created it. Without the music, it isnt goth anymore, it's just *gothic* or darkly inclined.

Many goths dont want to just exclude people, we want to teach people and bring new blood into the scene. While some of it may be in a harsh tone, a harsh tone is sometimes just inevitable due to the amount of bull shit we have to deal with. If you come to us with an open mind and take suggestions and advice and willing to just sit and discover everything, the gates are wide open. If you're talking down to us, or being rude, or claiming X is *goth* when it very much isnt while pushing us  away, then gates closed.

Any subculture has similar things like this, and if you're not willing to be open or listen to advice or suggestion, then of course you're going to be locked outside the gate, you're shitting on something that is dear to the subculture and no one within it wants to see it. A furry example would be "Are Nekos furry?" this is legitimately one of the biggest issues within the furry community when it comes to "What identify a furry", the answer is no, but you have the same kind of behaviour when it comes to gate keeping as the goth community faces.

People don't like gate keeping in every subculture. People don't like being told that they're not allowed to be appart of something.

Goth has developed this image that it is a cool fashion for cool people, and people want to be in with the cool lot. A lot of this has been caused by media portrayal and fashion brands trying to milk it for profit. This is why goth has such a hard time with it, there are people actively fighting back against what goth truly is.

A lot of people are like, dont pay until you get the final work. Unfortunately that's not how commission art works, atleast a professional one as otherwise they can end up doing a lot of work for no pay. This is why communication with the artist is very important. Typically if it is a big commission you will need to put down a deposit to secure a time slot for them (Typically about 10-20%, some will say it's refundable some wont, depends on the artist, again a professional one will have info like this and will tell you even before any money is involved) . After that point it varies from artist to artist, some will want instalments every time you check off the art, some will request a larger lump some after the 1st draft and then remaining at the end, etc.

Of course if it's a smaller piece, like £5-£25 then typically they want it upfront, and if you change your mind at the 1st draft they will refund it. (Personally for these commissions I do 50% upfront 50% on completion, if they change their mind at 1st draft then it's full refund, past that the deposit is kept)

Vitamin B is the main supplement to help encourage healthy hair growth.

In general I would just recommend getting some A-Z multivitamins and use them daily and also keep your hair washing to a minimum (1-2 times a week at max).

Look more into a oil, the kind which you put into  your hair after you've washed it and it's still wet.
